key_insight: A simple one‑shot probing technique can detect whether a domain is underrepresented in a vision–language foundation model's pretraining data, enabling assessment without labelled test sets.
problem_solved: Provides a practical way to evaluate VLFM coverage for novel, specialised, or Global South domains when labelled evaluation sets are unavailable, revealing potential blind spots before deployment or adaptation.
method: Provide a single representative example (image or caption) from the target domain and query the VLFM to obtain embeddings or retrieval/confidence outputs.
Compare the model's responses against reference distributions or contrasted prompts (in‑domain vs out‑of‑domain) to derive a representation score or underrepresentation signal.
Use simple calibration/contrastive checks (e.g., nearest‑neighbor ranks, similarity gaps, or prompt variants) to quantify how well the model recognises the domain from one example.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to rapidly screen foundation models for domain gaps with minimal data, guiding decisions on adaptation, data collection, or risk mitigation for underrepresented communities.
visual_elements: Schematic: one‑shot probe pipeline (single example → VLFM → embedding → comparison metric)
Bar chart: representation score across multiple domains (highlighting underrepresented Global South domains)
Heatmap: similarity/confidence of model responses across prompt variants or example types
Icon set: action outcomes (safe to use, fine‑tune, collect data, avoid deployment)
paper_title: Underrepresented in Foundation Model Pretraining Data? A One-Shot Probe
paper_authors: Chris Vorster, Mayug Maniparambil, Noel E. O'Connor, Noel Murphy, Derek Molloy
